tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

| Task | State at the cutoff | State now |
|---|---|---|
| **G4: conflict cards** (PR #18) | The agent had finished. I was about to hide the general Approve button on conflict cards, then merge. | PR #18 is still **open**. The Approve fix was committed to local `main` (`e4ddf7a`), not to the PR #18 branch. |
| **G5: Happiness Meter** | The agent failed at the session limit. | The UI was committed to local `main` (`238653f`), along with a `PLAN.md` update (`1c5735d`) that marks G4 and G5 as complete. Its worktree still holds an older, uncommitted draft. |
| **Dev server on port 3001** | Background task | Still running, for about 9 hours now. That's harmless. Port 3000 is your other app, which I didn't touch. |

## Problems with those 3 local commits

1. **The order is wrong.** `e4ddf7a` hides Approve on conflict cards, but the "Approve as global / market-specific" buttons only exist in PR #18, which isn't merged. If this went out now, conflict cards would have no way to be approved.
2. **It skips the PR rule.** G5 went straight onto `main` without review, and the browser tests weren't run.
3. **PLAN.md says G4 is complete, but it isn't merged.**
4. Typecheck passes. Lint shows only 3 unused-variable warnings, in `HappinessMeter.tsx` and `happiness.spec.ts`.

## New on GitHub since last night

- **#19 (Vishwa):** "Agentic voice workflow and BMW-style board design". It's large: +6,752 lines across 66 files. It touches every shared file, including `db.py`, `types.ts`, `gate.ts`, `DecisionCard.tsx`, `globals.css` and `Header.tsx`, so it will collide with your UI work.
- **#20 (Arjun):** a Kanban view for the Requirements tab, +291 lines. It overlaps with #18 and G5 in `vehicles/[code]/page.tsx`.

content.content:
PMs can now see how a requirement's evidence divides between observed comments, survey measures, inference and assumptions, and compare recurring customer issues across the vehicle portfolio. China shows zero observed comments instead of inheriting the US composition.

### Changes

- Complete Vishwa Phase 2: deterministic evidence mixes, regional stacked meter, `/portfolio` heatmap, and scoring slide plus five judge answers.
- Add `requirements.evidence_mix` and `requirements.evidence_mix_by_market` to the Python/TypeScript schema contract. The second column stores independently computed market mixes, avoiding estimates from the bounded quote sample.
- Add transactional, idempotent `uv run pmw evidence-mix` for existing databases. It preserves requirement fields, decisions, scores and history; missing metadata in legacy hosted databases displays a pending state.
- Show 212 customer-facing themes across F70/G60/G70, with exact sample counts, negative shares, recurring issues first, accessible legends and internal scrolling at 375px. The gate reads aggregate signal counts only; values are identical in every region.
- Integrate latest main (`73f49cd`), including survey-only market-conflict candidates, full signal membership, scope checks, photo matching and team naming. Survey-only candidates never borrow a comment signal.
- Publish the previously local professional workspace: sidebar and mobile navigation, independently scrolling requirement list/detail, review tabs, sticky actions, priority controls, exports and audit views. All existing features remain accessible.

The Phase 2 meter is composed beside the card by the vehicle page; it does not require another `DecisionCard.tsx` edit. For UI handoff: `EvidenceMeter({ mix: EvidenceMix | null, region: string })`, using `getRequirement(viewer, id).requirement.evidence_mix` and `viewer.label`. The earlier workspace redesign accounts for the card changes in this branch.

### Validation

- Isolated `uv run pmw build` and `uv run pmw verify`: pass across all eight source files; 61 requirements = 45 core + 10 quick wins + 6 survey-only candidates.
- Python: **69 tests and 66 subtests pass**.
- Node: **5 tests pass**, including score parity for every rebuilt requirement, region-filtered equipment evidence and approval coverage.
- TypeScript, ESLint and Next production build: pass.
- Playwright: **30 tests pass**. The three Phase 2 browser tests were rerun after the final mobile column-width adjustment and also pass.

content.text:
Arjun's Kanban is cleanly built, but it only partly follows our design language, and it changes how the screen works. I wouldn't merge it as it stands. I built it, screenshotted it next to the current inbox at desktop and phone width, and read the code. Build, typecheck and lint all pass.

## What fits our look

- It uses our colours, square corners, thin 1 px borders, light headline and BMW Blue for the selected item. There are no shadows or rounded cards.
- The car photo strip at the top uses the real price-list photos, and cars not sold in your region are greyed out, as on the home page.
- The phone layout has no sideways scrolling.

## Where it breaks our look

1. **The grid doesn't line up.** On the Requirements tab only, the content area widens to 1,600 px while the header stays at 1,280 px. On desktop, "BMW 7 Series" starts at 40 px from the left edge, but the PMW logo above it starts at 128 px. Your rebrand spec set a 1,280 px maximum.
2. **The tabs stop matching.** Requirements gets the photo strip and a small title, while the other tabs keep the dark full-width photo header. Switching tabs makes the top of the page jump to a different layout.
3. **The MoSCoW colours are gone.** You picked option B with red / orange / blue / grey groups. The board's columns are plain grey with sentence-case titles. Our spec puts labels in bold uppercase.
4. **The filter chips change style.** They're sentence case with a blue fill, while ours use dark fill and uppercase labels. They also lack the **Conflicts** chip, because the PR is older than #18.
5. **The cards show less.** They drop the Act / Validate tag, the car part ("Cockpit · Connectivity"), and the Quick win and Conflict badges. Priority and confidence get equal weight, which blurs the "priority ≠ confidence" story.
6. **"Review evidence ↗"** uses an external-link arrow for something that stays on the same page.

## How it works differently

- **The Decision Card moves below the board.** It now starts 1,294 px down on desktop instead of next to the list at 579 px. On a phone it starts at 4,523 px, on an 11,000 px page. The product manager has to scroll past every requirement to reach the evidence and the Approve / Challenge buttons, the main demo moment. The Gmail-style "list left, card right" layout, which you chose, is gone.
- The columns scroll inside themselves on wide screens, so the board has scroll areas inside the page scroll.
- The photo strip repeats the "7 Series / 5 Series / 1 Series" links already in the header.

## Code

**Good:**
- Search runs on the server, with input capped at 256 characters.
- MoSCoW groups reuse the shared `moscowFor` rules, and scores are never changed.
- Region privacy is untouched.
- Accessibility is solid: labelled groups, a hidden label on the search box, `aria-current` on the selected card.
- The changes to existing tests only update selectors, and 4 new tests are added.

**Problems:**
- **Hard-coded cars.** `RequirementModels.tsx` lists G70 / G60 / F70 and their photo paths by hand, although the `vehicles` table already stores each car's image. A 4th car wouldn't appear, which contradicts BMW's "works for other cars" requirement.
- **Extra database load.** Every Requirements page load calls `listVehicles()`, which runs 4 queries per car, including a full requirement list for each, just to draw the strip. That adds latency on Turso.
- **Merge conflict.** It conflicts with #18: the filter type has no `"conflict"` option.
- **AI mention.** The PR description mentions "subagents", against the no-AI-mentions rule.

## Recommendation

Keep the current inbox and take only the **search box** from #20. It's the one clear improvement, and it fits the existing list without layout changes.

If you prefer the Kanban, these must be fixed before merging:
- use the 1,280 px width
- bring back the MoSCoW colours, uppercase labels and badges
- add the Conflicts chip
- read the cars from the database
- keep the Decision Card beside the board on desktop, not below it

Separately, I found a small bug that's live now: the header requests `/brand/bmw-logo.svg`, which returns a 404, so a broken "BMW" image can flash on first load before the page hides it. Either add the logo file, or I can make the header leave it out until the file exists.

content.text:
**Yes, the Kanban is now the Requirements view.** I fixed everything from the review, then merged PR #20 and deployed it to https://product-minds-on-wheels.vercel.app.

## What I fixed

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Content was wider than the header (1,600 px vs 1,280 px) | Uses the same 1,280 px grid, so everything lines up under the PMW logo |
| Requirements tab had a different top section from the other tabs | Photo strip removed; every tab has the same car photo header |
| Hard-coded cars and extra database queries on every page load | Gone with the strip. The header already has the 7 / 5 / 1 Series links |
| No MoSCoW colours, sentence-case labels | Lanes have a red / orange / blue / grey top bar and bold uppercase labels like "MUST HAVE", plus their hint lines |
| Different chip style, no Conflicts chip | Same chips as the rest of the app, with Quick wins in blue and **Conflicts** in orange |
| Cards had lost the Act tag, the car part and the badges | All back, with priority shown large and confidence shown separately |
| Decision Card 1,294 px down the page | **On desktop the board stays on the left as a 2×2 grid, with the card beside it**, so the inbox feel is back. On phones the board comes first, a tap jumps to the card, and a link goes back to the board |
| Misleading ↗ arrow | Removed |
| AI mention in the PR description | Rewritten |
| Broken BMW logo flash | The logo only renders if `web/public/brand/bmw-logo.svg` existed when the site was built. Once you add the file, a redeploy shows it |

Search, from Arjun's version, is kept.

## Checks

- Typecheck, lint and production build pass.
- All **29 browser tests** pass. I updated Arjun's Kanban tests for the new layout and added checks that:
  - the card sits beside the board on desktop
  - the Conflicts filter works
  - the phone tap-to-card and back-to-board links work
  - there's no sideways scrolling at 390 px
- I checked the live site: the board, the lanes and the Conflicts chip are present, and the broken logo image and the photo strip are gone.

## Still open

- **PR #19 (Vishwa)** has its own workspace redesign and Kanban, so it now clashes directly with this one. When we pick it up, we'd keep his evidence meter, `/portfolio` page and scoring docs, and drop his layout and the voice agent, unless you decide otherwise.
- **PLAN.md** still needs the G4, G5 and Kanban updates.

content.content:
# PMW voice agent

A small floating microphone at the bottom centre of every page. Click it to talk to PMW; click again (or press Escape) to stop. The microphone animates while PMW listens and speaks. No transcript, panel or chat window is shown; only a brief message appears if voice cannot start.

## Setup

1. In `web/.env.local`, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (server only; never prefix with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`). Optional: `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` (default `gpt-realtime`) and `OPENAI_REALTIME_VOICE` (default `marin`).
2. Run `npm run dev` and open <http://localhost:3000>. Allow microphone access when asked.

Without a key the app and tests still run; clicking the microphone shows a short configuration message.

## How it works

- `POST /api/voice/session` (same-origin only) mints a short-lived OpenAI Realtime client secret. The agent's prompt, tools and turn detection are fixed there, server-side. The API key never reaches the browser.
- `lib/voice/realtime.ts` connects the browser to OpenAI over WebRTC. Audio streams directly; transcripts and tool calls use the data channel. Server voice-activity detection allows natural turn-taking and interrupting PMW mid-sentence.
- `components/VoiceAgent.tsx` renders the microphone and the confirmation dialog. Final user transcripts are kept (not shown) as the audited spoken request. It sends the current page context (page, model, selected requirement, region) to the agent on start and on every navigation.
- Every tool call goes to `POST /api/voice/tools`, which runs existing PMW queries and actions (`lib/voice/server.ts`) with the viewer's region filter. Each call is written to the audit trail twice — the spoken request before execution and the result after — and fails closed if the audit write fails.
- Sessions end after 90 seconds of inactivity or when the tab is hidden.

## Tools

| Tool | PMW integration |
| --- | --- |
| `navigate(page, model?, view?)` | Home, portfolio, workflow, audit trail, or a vehicle's requirements / decision matrix / signals / data health |
| `list_vehicles` | `listVehicles` — programs, comments, requirements, decisions awaiting review |
| `find_requirements(model, filter?, query?)` | `listRequirements` filtered by status, quadrant, quick wins, conflicts or keyword |
| `open_requirement(id)` | `getRequirement`, Evidence tab |
| `explain_score(id)` | Priority and confidence factors, evidence mix, Scoring tab |
| `read_customer_quotes(id, n)` | Verbatim, region-permitted comments |
| `summarize_feedback(model)` | `listSignals` top topics + approval coverage per market |
| `run_challenge(id)` | Existing Evidence Challenger (`applyAction: challenge`) |
| `critical_issues(model?)` | High-priority undecided requirements, challenged evidence, conflicts, missing voices, critical data issues |
| `daily_briefing` | Pending decisions, gaps, conflicts since the previous briefing |
| `show_missing_voices(model)` | Feedback vs. sales representation |
| `audit_trail(id? / model?)` | `auditFor` / `auditLog` |
| `portfolio_overview` | Cross-model recurring themes |
| `request_decision(id, decision)` | Proposal only — see below |

Team strategy weights cannot be changed by voice.

## Decisions need a click

`request_decision` never changes anything. It stores a one-use, five-minute proposal tied to the browser and region and opens an on-screen dialog. Only clicking **Confirm** calls `POST /api/voice/confirm`, which is not in the agent's tool list. The token is never sent to the model, a spoken "yes" cannot confirm, and stale or expired proposals are refused. Confirmations and cancellations are logged in the audit trail.

## Tests

- `npm run test:voice` — unit tests for the agent UI and the session route.
- `npx playwright test tests/voice.spec.ts` — tool APIs, region gating, audit logging, confirmation flow and the microphone's layout against the real database.

# PMW voice agent

A small floating microphone at the bottom centre of every page. Click it to talk to PMW; click again (or press Escape) to stop. The microphone animates while PMW listens and speaks. No transcript, panel or chat window is shown; only a brief message appears if voice cannot start.

## Setup

1. In `web/.env.local`, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (server only; never prefix with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`). Optional: `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` (default `gpt-realtime`) and `OPENAI_REALTIME_VOICE` (default `marin`).
2. Run `npm run dev` and open <http://localhost:3000>. Allow microphone access when asked.

Without a key the app and tests still run; clicking the microphone shows a short configuration message.

## How it works

- `POST /api/voice/session` (same-origin only) mints a short-lived OpenAI Realtime client secret. The agent's prompt, tools and turn detection are fixed there, server-side. The API key never reaches the browser.
- `lib/voice/realtime.ts` connects the browser to OpenAI over WebRTC. Audio streams directly; transcripts and tool calls use the data channel. Server voice-activity detection allows natural turn-taking and interrupting PMW mid-sentence.
- `components/VoiceAgent.tsx` renders the microphone and the confirmation dialog. Final user transcripts are kept (not shown) as the audited spoken request. It sends the current page context (page, model, selected requirement, region) to the agent on start and on every navigation.
- Every tool call goes to `POST /api/voice/tools`, which runs existing PMW queries and actions (`lib/voice/server.ts`) with the viewer's region filter. Each call is written to the audit trail twice — the spoken request before execution and the result after — and fails closed if the audit write fails.
- Sessions end after 90 seconds of inactivity or when the tab is hidden.

## Tools

| Tool | PMW integration |
| --- | --- |
| `navigate(page, model?, view?)` | Home, portfolio, workflow, audit trail, or a vehicle's requirements / decision matrix / signals / data health |
| `list_vehicles` | `listVehicles` — programs, comments, requirements, decisions awaiting review |
| `find_requirements(model, filter?, query?)` | `listRequirements` filtered by status, quadrant, quick wins, conflicts or keyword |
| `open_requirement(id)` | `getRequirement`, Evidence tab |
| `explain_score(id)` | Priority and confidence factors, evidence mix, Scoring tab |
| `read_customer_quotes(id, n)` | Verbatim, region-permitted comments |
| `summarize_feedback(model)` | `listSignals` top topics + approval coverage per market |
| `run_challenge(id)` | Existing Evidence Challenger (`applyAction: challenge`) |
| `critical_issues(model?)` | High-priority undecided requirements, challenged evidence, conflicts, missing voices, critical data issues |
| `daily_briefing` | Pending decisions, gaps, conflicts since the previous briefing |
| `show_missing_voices(model)` | Feedback vs. sales representation |
| `audit_trail(id? / model?)` | `auditFor` / `auditLog` |
| `portfolio_overview` | Cross-model recurring themes |
| `request_decision(id, decision)` | Proposal only — see below |

Team strategy weights cannot be changed by voice.

## Decisions need a click

`request_decision` never changes anything. It stores a one-use, five-minute proposal tied to the browser and region and opens an on-screen dialog. Only clicking **Confirm** calls `POST /api/voice/confirm`, which is not in the agent's tool list. The token is never sent to the model, a spoken "yes" cannot confirm, and stale or expired proposals are refused. Confirmations and cancellations are logged in the audit trail.

## Tests

- `npm run test:voice` — unit tests for the agent UI and the session route.
- `npx playwright test tests/voice.spec.ts` — tool APIs, region gating, audit logging, confirmation flow and the microphone's layout against the real database.

content.text:
`feature_v` has **7 commits** since it split from `main` at #17. Three of them are Vishwa merging `main` into his branch. The real work is in four:

| Commit | Time | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `c652427` | Sat 23:25 | Redesigns the whole app as a "compact workspace" |
| `4fdf301` | Sun 00:37 | Evidence mix data + `/portfolio` |
| `563395d` | Sun 06:23 | Kanban workspace + OpenAI voice agent (the big one: +4,883 lines) |
| `7c7559b` | Sun 07:38 | Voice workflow polish + "BMW-style board design" |

## New features

1. **Evidence vs. assumption meter** (`EvidenceMeter.tsx`, `pipeline/pmw/evidence_mix.py`). Each requirement shows how its evidence splits into observed comments / survey / AI inference / assumptions, per market, and China correctly shows 0 observed. This is his planned Phase 2 task and adds two new database columns.
2. **`/portfolio` page.** It's a heatmap of 212 customer themes across the 1, 5 and 7 Series. Also from his Phase 2 plan.
3. **Scoring slide + judge answers** (`docs/pitch/scoring.md`). This fills the placeholder in the deck.
4. **Kanban "board" everywhere.** The **home page becomes a board across all cars**, and each car page gets a new default **Board** tab ahead of Requirements. Clicking a card opens it in a side panel (`RequirementDrawer`).
5. **Decision Card in tabs** (`ReviewTabs`). All the same sections remain (evidence, survey, ladder, priority, confidence, assumptions, audit), now arranged as tabs.
6. **OpenAI Realtime voice agent.** A floating microphone on **every page** that can:
   - navigate pages
   - find and open requirements
   - explain scores
   - **read customer quotes aloud**
   - run Challenge
   - give a daily briefing
   - propose a decision, which needs an on-screen Confirm click

   Every voice action is logged in the audit trail. It needs `OPENAI_API_KEY`, and it adds test tools (Vitest, jsdom, Testing Library).
7. **Sidebar navigation** replaces the top menu, with Portfolio, Workflow and Audit in it.

## Existing things it removes or changes

**Removed outright:**
- **The home page with the three car photos.** Its intro, the 1-second entrance, the "Not sold in your region" lanes and the "Thin evidence" labels are all replaced by the board.
- **"for BMW Group · Hackathon Prototype"**, the label your rebrand spec required.
- **The `--bmw-*` colour variables** from your spec.

**Changed away from our design:**
- **Colours:** text goes from BMW's neutral dark grey (#262626) to a blue-slate (#202b3c), with blue-grey lines and backgrounds.
- **Square corners:** about 30 rounded corners of 4–12 px, plus pill shapes, against your 0–2 px rule.
- **The Requirements screen:** the Board tab and drawer bring back a second Kanban, so it competes with Arjun's version (#20), which we just merged.
- **Export:** CSV and JSON move into a dropdown.

**Missing because the branch predates them** (merging as-is would undo them):
- **#18:** Conflicts chip, "Global or market-specific" block, hidden Approve on conflict cards
- **#21:** Happiness Meter
- **#20:** the fixed Kanban
- the build-time logo fix

## Risks with the voice agent

- **BMW customer comments get sent to OpenAI.** "Read customer quotes" passes real verbatims to a third-party AI service, and the microphone audio goes there too. That ends the site's "no third-party requests" promise, and you should check the hackathon's data rules first.
- **Voice can change data without a click.** Decisions need an on-screen Confirm, but **Challenge runs by voice alone**, and Challenge lowers confidence.
- It's one more thing that can fail during a live demo (key, microphone permission, Wi-Fi).

## My suggestion

Take the parts that fill gaps in our plan:
- the evidence meter
- `/portfolio`
- the scoring docs

Leave out:
- the layout redesign (sidebar, board home, tabs, colours, rounded corners)
- the voice agent

That keeps your rebrand and the merged Kanban intact. If you agree, I'll bring those three parts in as a new PR on top of the current `main`, and leave the rest on `feature_v`.

# PMW: Deep Architecture Guide

**Product Minds on Wheels (PMW)** turns BMW customer evidence into prioritised, traceable requirements for the next vehicle generation. The product manager (PM) makes every decision, and every step is recorded.

This guide covers the whole system end to end. For every screen it shows what you see, what each number means, which function produces it and which database table it comes from. File references are relative to the repo root (`PMW-Product-Minds-on-Wheels-/`).

lines: +Vishwa Phase 2 adds a region-aware evidence/assumption meter and `/portfolio`, a theme-by-vehicle heatmap with
+aggregate counts only. The additive `requirements.evidence_mix` and `evidence_mix_by_market` columns can be
+backfilled without replacing decisions: back up the existing database, then run `uv run pmw evidence-mix` from
+`pipeline`. A full rebuild is still needed to regenerate upstream source changes. See the [Phase 2 delivery and
Regression checks: `cd pipeline && uv run --extra llm python -m unittest discover -s tests -v`, then
`cd ../web && node --test scripts/test-equipment-evidence.mjs scripts/test-happiness.mjs scripts/test-score.mjs && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build`.
Run `npm run test:e2e` after building; it uses a separate copy of the local database.
Implementation, checks and limitations: [Vishwa pipeline handoff](docs/VISHWA_IMPLEMENTATION.md).

+Optional voice agent (OpenAI Realtime): [setup, tools and safety](docs/VOICE_COPILOT.md). Set the server-side `OPENAI_API_KEY` in `web/.env.local`, then click the small microphone at the bottom of any page to talk to PMW in English or German.
+Branch: `feature_v` (as requested). Includes the professional workspace and the latest merged team work from
+`main` at `73f49cd`. The existing review actions, exports, region restrictions, ranking controls and audit trail
+remain available. The Phase 2 meter integration does not edit `DecisionCard.tsx`: the vehicle page composes the
+meter immediately above the card. This branch also retains the earlier workspace redesign, which introduced
+review tabs in that card. The sidebar/mobile navigation includes the new portfolio route.
+| P2-1 | Deterministic global and market evidence mixes; stacked meter; legacy backfill; pipeline and browser checks |
+| P2-2 | `/portfolio`: theme × vehicle heatmap, sample counts, recurring themes, links to signals, internal mobile scrolling |
+| P2-3 | Skipped as allowed: no Anthropic API key configured. Reviewed templates retained; no fabricated live cache or comparison |
+| P2-4 | [Scoring slide and five formula answers](pitch/scoring.md), including the merged survey-only scoring exception |
+- `evidence_mix TEXT`: JSON `{observed, survey, inferred, assumed}`, normalized to one. Nullable solely for an
+  existing database awaiting backfill; all requirements in a completed build have a value.
+- `evidence_mix_by_market TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'`: the same four-key mix for US, EU, CN and ROW. These are
+  computed by the pipeline, so the web app never estimates regional composition from a small displayed quote sample.
+`settings.evidence_mix_rule` records `evidence-mix:v1` and its explanation. The rule is documented next to the
+[implementation](../pipeline/pmw/evidence_mix.py). It uses distinct comment IDs and survey measure identities,
+tracks provisional labels and theme merging, respects text exclusions, and uses only feature-specific wishes for
+quick wins. Survey-only conflict candidates never borrow a comment signal. A batched source scan avoids a query
+per requirement and market. The mix describes the draft's provenance, not causal proof or measured truth fractions.
+For an existing SQLite database, make a SQLite backup, set `PMW_DB` to that file's absolute path if needed, then run:
+This command adds columns, fills the mix and writes an aggregate audit event in one transaction. It does not
+rebuild, change requirement IDs, overwrite PM wording/status/scores, reset strategy weights, or delete history.
+It is idempotent and rolls back the additive schema if computation fails. It does not regenerate old requirements
+from newly changed upstream source rules; a full `pmw build` is still a fresh-demo rebuild that erases decisions.
+For this delivery, the local database was backed up to `db/pmw-before-phase2-20261010-223932.sqlite` and all
+131 existing requirements were enriched; every original field and all 807 pre-existing audit events were checked
+for equality. An isolated rebuild in `db/pmw-phase2-verify.sqlite` exercises the latest pipeline instead: 61
+requirements (45 core, 10 equipment quick wins, 6 survey-only market conflicts) from all eight supplied files.
+Database files and backups are ignored by Git. The hosted Turso database has not been replaced; its maintainer
+must apply the additive backfill to a current snapshot before using the meter there. An older hosted schema
+continues rendering with “Evidence composition is pending for this dataset” instead of invented percentages.
+Props: `mix: EvidenceMix | null`, `region: string`. Use the requirement returned by `getRequirement(viewer, id)`;
+`gate.ts` selects the viewer's precomputed mix. Never pair the global mix with a regional label. The component is
+server-compatible, takes no raw customer text, includes a textual legend and accessible bar description, and
+displays rounded percentages that total 100. The expandable explanation distinguishes provenance from confidence.
+For China, observed comments are zero even when US comments inform the global draft. No changes to DecisionCard
+are required for the integration delivered here.
+`portfolio()` is an async gate read of only vehicle labels and in-scope signal summary counts. The page does not
+fetch comment text, IDs or dominant-issue snippets. Its values are identical across viewer regions. “No evidence”
+is distinct from 0% negative. Counts are deduplicated within a theme, but cannot be added across themes.
+- Isolated `uv run pmw build` and `uv run pmw verify`: pass, all eight source files checked.
+- `uv run --with pytest pytest -q tests`: 69 tests plus 66 subtests pass, including normalization, China,
+  quick wins, survey-only candidates, tamper detection, migration preservation and rollback.
+- Node score, equipment-evidence and happiness checks: 5 pass; score parity covers all 61 rebuilt requirements.
+- Next route type generation, TypeScript, ESLint and production build pass.
+- Browser checks: 30 pass, including regional meter values/rounding, aggregate-only heatmap parity across all five regions,
+  vehicle links, 375px scrolling, and the existing PM workflow, exports, weights, privacy and keyboard navigation.
+Screenshots from the isolated production build are in [reports/vishwa-phase2](reports/vishwa-phase2).
+The browser test fixture is copied to `db/pmw-smoke-run.sqlite`; tests never mutate the working database.

+A small floating microphone at the bottom centre of every page. Click it to talk to PMW; click again (or press Escape) to stop. The microphone animates while PMW listens and speaks. No transcript, panel or chat window is shown; only a brief message appears if voice cannot start.

+1. In `web/.env.local`, set `OPENAI_API_KEY` (server only; never prefix with `NEXT_PUBLIC_`). Optional: `OPENAI_REALTIME_MODEL` (default `gpt-realtime`) and `OPENAI_REALTIME_VOICE` (default `marin`).
+2. Run `npm run dev` and open <http://localhost:3000>. Allow microphone access when asked.
+Without a key the app and tests still run; clicking the microphone shows a short configuration message.

+- `POST /api/voice/session` (same-origin only) mints a short-lived OpenAI Realtime client secret. The agent's prompt, tools and turn detection are fixed there, server-side. The API key never reaches the browser.

+- `lib/voice/realtime.ts` connects the browser to OpenAI over WebRTC. Audio streams directly; transcripts and tool calls use the data channel. Server voice-activity detection allows natural turn-taking and interrupting PMW mid-sentence.

+- `components/VoiceAgent.tsx` renders the microphone and the confirmation dialog. Final user transcripts are kept (not shown) as the audited spoken request. It sends the current page context (page, model, selected requirement, region) to the agent on start and on every navigation.

+- Every tool call goes to `POST /api/voice/tools`, which runs existing PMW queries and actions (`lib/voice/server.ts`) with the viewer's region filter. Each call is written to the audit trail twice — the spoken request before execution and the result after — and fails closed if the audit write fails.
+- Sessions end after 90 seconds of inactivity or when the tab is hidden.
+| `navigate(page, model?, view?)` | Home, portfolio, workflow, audit trail, or a vehicle's requirements / decision matrix / signals / data health |
+| `list_vehicles` | `listVehicles` — programs, comments, requirements, decisions awaiting review |
+| `find_requirements(model, filter?, query?)` | `listRequirements` filtered by status, quadrant, quick wins, conflicts or keyword |
+| `explain_score(id)` | Priority and confidence factors, evidence mix, Scoring tab |
+| `summarize_feedback(model)` | `listSignals` top topics + approval coverage per market |
+| `critical_issues(model?)` | High-priority undecided requirements, challenged evidence, conflicts, missing voices, critical data issues |
+| `daily_briefing` | Pending decisions, gaps, conflicts since the previous briefing |
+Team strategy weights cannot be changed by voice.

+`request_decision` never changes anything. It stores a one-use, five-minute proposal tied to the browser and region and opens an on-screen dialog. Only clicking **Confirm** calls `POST /api/voice/confirm`, which is not in the agent's tool list. The token is never sent to the model, a spoken "yes" cannot confirm, and stale or expired proposals are refused. Confirmations and cancellations are logged in the audit trail.
+- `npm run test:voice` — unit tests for the agent UI and the session route.
+- `npx playwright test tests/voice.spec.ts` — tool APIs, region gating, audit logging, confirmation flow and the microphone's layout against the real database.
+**Slide:** Priority asks “How much does this matter?” Confidence asks “How strong is the evidence?”
+Both are deterministic weighted averages on a 0–100 scale. The model writes hypotheses and explanations;
+it cannot set a score, weight, threshold, or evidence mix.
+| Priority factor | Default weight | Confidence factor | Default weight |
+| Market relevance (2030 sales shares) | 20% | Market representation | 20% |
+Default boundaries: priority **55**, confidence **58**. High/high → Act; high/low → Validate first;
+low/high → Monitor; low/low → Park. PMs can preview and apply different priority weights with a reason;
+the application logs the change and recomputes ranking. Confidence stays independent of strategy weights.
+**Challenge** identifies concentration, missing markets, small samples and conflicting evidence, then applies
+published confidence penalties. It explains the result and records the change; priority stays unchanged.
+The PM still approves, edits, rejects or requests validation. No score is a probability or an automatic approval.
+**Speaker note:** “Numbers come from code; words come from the model or reviewed templates. We show every
+factor, source, assumption and change. The evidence meter separates comments, surveys, inference and assumptions;
+it is a provenance index, not another confidence score. China can have survey evidence and zero observed comments.”
+### 1. Why these weights and boundaries? Are they statistically validated?
+They are explicit prototype strategy choices, not fitted or validated predictions. Impact and repeat evidence
+receive 60% of priority; a competitor name alone receives only 5%. Quantity and diversity share half of confidence.
+55 matches the existing Should-have priority boundary; 58 approximates a reference evidence case with 30 comments,
+two balanced sources, partial representation/agreement and unknown dates. Production calibration needs historical
+PM decisions and outcome validation. The sensitivity panel varies each priority weight by ±20%, one at a time,
+renormalizes, and flags a boundary crossing. That range is not a statistical confidence interval.
+### 2. How do you stop a high-volume topic or the US sample dominating?
+Frequency uses `min(1, log1p(negative comments) / max(1, log1p(largest negative count)))`, relative to that vehicle's
+selected themes. Impact is `0.6 × negative share + 0.4 × severity`. IDs are deduplicated within each theme; IDs are
+not necessarily unique people. Quantity saturates at `min(1, log10(n + 1) / 2)`. Source diversity uses the inverse
+sum of squared source shares, plus one when mapped survey evidence exists, divided by four and capped at one.
+Representation compares comment market shares with **2025** sales shares; a survey in a market with fewer than
+three comments gets only partial credit (30% of that market's sales share). These measures expose bias; they do
+not correct the sample into a representative population. Missing voices remain visible.
+### 3. How do surveys, competitors and the 2030 assumptions affect priority and confidence?
+Market relevance sums **2030** sales shares for markets with at least three topic comments or a mapped survey gap
+of at least 0.3. Competitive pressure is `min(1, competitor mentions / max(6, 0.15 × comments))`. Future relevance
+is a reviewed topic rule (0.70 for the configured successor-relevant topics, otherwise 0.45); it is neither a
+demand forecast nor a model-generated value. Confidence agreement starts at 0.4 plus 0.6 times the fraction of
+survey measures with gap ≥0.3 (0.5 if none), then subtracts half the share of comments that exclusively praise
+the topic. Recency is 0.5 because dates are absent. A feature quick win uses its specific wishing comments and
+no broad-topic survey as proof of demand. All these details are available beside each factor in the app.
+### 4. What exactly does Challenge change, and can it keep lowering confidence?
+Challenge subtracts deterministic penalties from the original confidence: 8 for ≥70% of comments from one
+market; 6 for each market with ≥15% of 2025 sales and zero comments; 8 for fewer than 30 comments; 6 if ≥20% praise
+the topic; 8 if every mapped survey gap is below 0.2; 4 if no survey maps; 4 for ≥80% of evidence from one source.
+The result is clamped at zero. These penalties can overlap; they are a conservative review heuristic, not
+independent probabilities. The action is applied once, with audit entries, and may move the quadrant. It neither
+changes priority nor decides for the PM. Repeated clicks do not stack penalties.
+### 5. Does “40% observed” mean 40% of the requirement has been proven?
+No. Evidence composition v1 allocates transparent units: observed comments get up to four, reaching the cap at
+30 distinct IDs; distinct mapped survey measures get one each, capped at four. Inference gets two for causal
+hypothesis and requirement translation, one extra if multiple source topics were merged, and up to one for the
+fraction of provisionally labelled comments. Assumptions get one for successor relevance and another for equipment
+transfer in quick wins. Normalize to one, with deterministic rounding. These are design choices, not measured
+truth fractions. Each market is computed independently, so China's observed portion is zero with this dataset.
+Surveys may disagree with the draft; their direction belongs in the agreement score and evidence panel. Editing
+the prose does not validate the hypothesis or change the draft's underlying provenance.
+The merged market-conflict builder uses the same weight sets but a separate, explicit factor mapping because
+these candidates have no comment signal. Impact is the largest of the two survey gaps; frequency, quantity and
+competitive pressure are zero (unknown, not invented). Market relevance and representation use the combined
+**2025** CN/EU sales share. Future relevance is 0.45, source diversity and agreement are each 0.25, and recency is
+0.5. Challenge subtracts 8 for unknown sample sizes and 6 for absent comment triangulation. The evidence meter
+counts only the supplied survey rows plus inference and successor assumptions, even for the all-markets viewer.
+See [market_requirements.py](../../pipeline/pmw/market_requirements.py). Their scores are review prompts, not
+evidence that CN and EU need different products.
+Live Anthropic generation was skipped for this delivery because no key was configured. Reviewed templates remain
+labelled as such; no live before/after comparison or generated cache is claimed.
+Captured from the production build using the isolated, freshly rebuilt dataset. Desktop: 1440 × 900;
+mobile: 375 × 900. The viewer is China, so these screenshots contain aggregate evidence without raw US comments.

+| Evidence and assumptions | ![China evidence mix at 1440px](evidence-desktop.png) | ![China evidence mix at 375px](evidence-mobile.png) |

+mix, verify all five regions have identical heatmap counts, and exercise horizontal keyboard scrolling and
+navigation from every vehicle column. [Delivery notes and migration](../../PHASE2_VISHWA.md).

+/* Decision Card tabs (Overview / Evidence / Scoring / Activity): same look as the vehicle view tabs. */
+.review-tablist { display: flex; gap: 28px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line); overflow-x: auto; }

+.review-tablist button { padding: 12px 0; border-bottom: 2px solid transparent; margin-bottom: -1px; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 700; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--color-ink-3); white-space: nowrap; }
+.review-tabpanel:not([hidden]) { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 24px; padding-top: 24px; }
+/* Voice agent: one microphone, bottom right. Square panels, BMW Blue only. */
+.voice-agent { position: fixed; right: 24px; bottom: max(24px, env(safe-area-inset-bottom)); z-index: 60; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: flex-end; pointer-events: none; }

+.voice-mic { position: relative; width: 52px; height: 52px; border-radius: 50%; display: grid; place-items: center; color: #fff; background: var(--color-blue); pointer-events: auto; transition: background-color .15s ease, transform .15s ease; }
+.voice-glow { position: absolute; inset: -6px; z-index: 0; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--color-blue); opacity: 0; transition: opacity .3s ease; }
+.voice-bars { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 3px; height: 20px; }

content.text:
Vishwa's decision board is now on the branch, as a **Decisions** tab on each car page next to Requirements. It's pushed to PR #22, and there's a new preview link (previews get a fresh URL each time):

**https://product-minds-on-wheels-fwj7ql5bp-gokul-rajan-s-projects.vercel.app**

Go to the 7 Series and open the **Decisions** tab.

**What it does:**
- **Five columns by decision status:** To Review, Needs Validation, Edited / Re-review, Approved and Rejected. The top shows counts for Awaiting review, Needs validation, Approved and Total.
- **Each card** shows its MoSCoW priority in colour, the Act / Quick win / Conflict badges, priority and confidence, the number of customer comments, and whether it has been challenged.
- **Clicking a card** opens its full Decision Card, with evidence, tabs, Approve and Challenge.
- **"Move to…"** on each card moves it to another column, with the same rules as Vishwa's version:
  - Reject and Validate need a reason; the dialog won't save without one.
  - An approved or rejected card has to go back to To Review (Reopen) before it can get a new decision.
  - Every move goes into the audit trail.
- The voice agent can open this tab too ("show me the decisions for the 7 Series").
- It uses our styling: square corners, BMW palette, uppercase labels.

**Different from Vishwa's version:**
- Clicking a card opens our Decision Card instead of his slide-in drawer.
- Cards move with the "Move to…" menu, not drag-and-drop.
- The home page is unchanged.

**Checks:** typecheck, lint, build and **49 / 49 browser tests** pass. That includes 3 new tests: cards land in the column matching their database status; a reject without a reason is refused, while one with a reason is saved and audited; and reopening, the card link and phone width all work. I also checked the new preview: the Decisions tab loads with its columns and menus.

**On the preview:** anything you move there also changes the live site's data. The backup from this morning is still in `BMW Hackathon/backups/`, so I can restore it or reset the database whenever you want.

# walk top-level, keeping media wrappers
out=[]; i=0; depth=0; buf=''
def blocks(s):
    i=0; n=len(s)
    while i<n:
        j=s.find('{',i)
        if j<0: break
        sel=s[i:j].strip(); d=1; k=j+1
        while d and k<n:
            if s[k]=='{': d+=1
            elif s[k]=='}': d-=1
            k+=1
        yield sel, s[j+1:k-1]; i=k
keep=re.compile(r'\.(board|drawer|rec-dot|card-flag|move-)')
res=[]
for sel,body in blocks(css):
    if sel.startswith('@media') or sel.startswith('@supports'):
        inner=[f"  {s2} {{{b2}}}" for s2,b2 in blocks(body) if keep.search(s2)]
        if inner: res.append(sel+" {\n"+"\n".join(inner)+"\n}")
    elif sel.startswith('@keyframes'):
        if 'drawer' in sel or 'agent-pulse' in sel: res.append(f"{sel} {{{body}}}")
    elif keep.search(sel):
        res.append(f"{sel} {{{body}}}")
open('/tmp/board.css','w').write("\n".join(res))
print(len(res), "rules,", sum(len(r) for r in res), "chars")

+/* Kanban requirements board: full-height board, compact KPIs and filters in a right sidebar */
+.board-content { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; padding: 12px 20px 0; }
+.board-page, .board-workspace { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
+.board-head { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px 12px; margin-bottom: 10px; }
+.board-heading { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: baseline; gap: 2px 12px; min-width: 0; }
+.board-heading .board-ranking { padding: 2px 8px; border-left: 2px solid var(--color-blue); background: var(--color-monitor-soft); color: var(--color-ink-2); }
+.board-heading .board-availability { flex-basis: 100%; padding: 4px 10px; border-left: 2px solid var(--color-validate); background: var(--color-validate-soft); color: var(--color-ink-2); }
+.board-layout-toggle { display: flex; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; overflow: hidden; }
+.board-layout-toggle button { height: 30px; padding: 0 12px; font-size: 13px; color: var(--color-ink-2); background: #fff; }
+.board-notice { margin-bottom: 8px; padding: 6px 12px; border-left: 2px solid var(--color-blue); background: var(--color-monitor-soft); font-size: 13px; }
+.board-shell { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 260px; gap: 14px; }
+.board-main { min-width: 0; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; }
+.board-columns { flex: 1; min-height: 0; display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(256px, 1fr)); gap: 10px; overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: hidden; padding-bottom: 6px; }

+.board-column { min-width: 0; min-height: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; overflow: hidden; background: #f6f6f6; border: 1px solid transparent; border-radius: 0; transition: background .15s ease, border-color .15s ease; }
+.board-column.is-over { background: var(--color-monitor-soft); border-color: var(--color-blue); border-style: dashed; }
+.board-column-head { flex: none; display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 10px 12px 2px; }

+.board-count { min-width: 24px; padding: 1px 8px; border-radius: 0; background: #fff; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 600; text-align: center; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; color: var(--color-ink-2); }
+.board-column-hint { flex: none; padding: 0 12px 8px; font-size: 11px; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+.board-cards { flex: 1; min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 8px; padding: 0 8px 84px; }
+.board-empty { padding: 12px 8px; text-align: center; font-size: 12px; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+.board-side { min-height: 0; overflow-y: auto; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 12px; padding-bottom: 84px; }
+.board-kpis { display: flex; flex-direction: column; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; }
+.board-kpis > div { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 14px; }
+.board-kpis dd { font-size: 20px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: -.02em; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; }
+.board-filters { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 10px; padding: 12px 14px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; }
+.board-filters label { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 4px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-ink-3); }

+.board-filters select, .board-filters input { width: 100%; height: 30px; padding: 0 8px; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; background: #fff; font-size: 13px; color: var(--color-ink); }
+.board-filters select:focus, .board-filters input:focus { outline: 2px solid var(--color-blue); outline-offset: 0; }

+  .board-side { display: none; position: fixed; top: 56px; right: 0; bottom: 0; z-index: 46; width: 300px; max-width: 100%; padding: 12px 12px 84px; background: var(--color-mist); border-left: 1px solid var(--color-line); box-shadow: none; }
+  .board-side-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; }
+  .board-side-close { padding: 0 8px; border-radius: 0; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1.2; color: var(--color-ink-3); }

+.board-card { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 6px; padding: 10px 12px 10px 14px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none; cursor: grab; transition: box-shadow .15s ease, transform .15s ease, opacity .15s ease; }
+.board-card::before { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 0; top: 10px; bottom: 10px; width: 3px; border-radius: 0; background: var(--color-line); }
+.board-card-top { display: flex; align-items: flex-start; justify-content: space-between; gap: 6px; }
+.board-card-title { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.35; color: var(--color-ink); display: -webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp: 2; -webkit-box-orient: vertical; overflow: hidden; }
+.board-card-move { flex: none; width: 24px; height: 22px; border-radius: 0; color: var(--color-ink-3); font-size: 15px; line-height: 1; }

+.board-move-menu { position: absolute; right: 8px; top: 34px; z-index: 5; display: flex; flex-direction: column; min-width: 190px; padding: 4px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--color-line); border-radius: 0; box-shadow: none; }
+.board-move-menu button { padding: 7px 10px; border-radius: 0; text-align: left; font-size: 13px; }
+.board-card-scores dd span { margin-left: 1px; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 400; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+.board-card-link { align-self: flex-start; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-blue); }
+.board-list th { padding: 10px 12px; text-align: left; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--color-ink-3); border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line); }
+.board-list td { padding: 10px 12px; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line); vertical-align: top; }

+.drawer-panel { position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: min(760px, 100%); background: var(--color-mist); border-left: 1px solid var(--color-line); box-shadow: none; animation: drawer-in .2s ease-out; outline: none; }
+.drawer-bar { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; padding: 10px 16px; background: #fff; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--color-line); }
+.drawer-close { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; height: 30px; padding: 0 10px; border-radius: 0; font-size: 22px; line-height: 1; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+@keyframes drawer-in { from { transform: translateX(24px); opacity: 0; } to { transform: none; opacity: 1; } }
+.drawer-close { position: absolute; right: 12px; top: 24px; width: 32px; height: 32px; font-size: 24px; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+.board-card[data-agent=investigating] { border-color: var(--color-blue); box-shadow: none; animation: agent-pulse 1.2s ease-in-out infinite; }
+.board-column-head h2, .board-kpis dt, .board-filters label { font-size: 10.5px; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: .08em; text-transform: uppercase; }
+.board-filters select, .board-filters input { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 400; letter-spacing: 0; text-transform: none; color: var(--color-ink); }
+/* Kanban: quiet grey columns, white cards, 4px side line in the AI recommendation colour */
+.board-card { padding-left: 16px; border-color: #e6e6e6; box-shadow: none; transition: box-shadow .18s ease, transform .18s ease, border-color .18s ease; }
+.board-legend { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 4px 14px; font-size: 11px; color: var(--color-ink-3); }
+.board-legend li { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; }
+.board-legend li::before { content: ""; width: 4px; height: 12px; background: currentColor; }
+/* PMW overrides for Vishwa's board: it sits in our page (sidebar + 72px header), so the summary and
+   filters run in a band above the columns and the five columns share the width instead of scrolling. */
+.board-side { order: -1; display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); gap: 12px; overflow: visible; padding-bottom: 0; position: static; }
+.board-filters { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(170px, 1fr)); gap: 12px; }
+.board-columns { grid-template-columns: repeat(5, minmax(190px, 1fr)); overflow-x: auto; overflow-y: visible; }
+  .board-side { display: grid; position: static; width: auto; padding: 0; background: none; border: 0; }

# Cloover 4 - Minerva - Voice-First Sales Engine

A minimalist, voice-first autonomous sales assistant called Minerva. Minerva acts as a hands-free sales coach that intelligently reads customer's schedule for the day and extracts data like data (Location, Name, Product Interest) and leverages a powerful multi-agent AI pipeline to generate real-time, personalized sales playbooks.

## 🚀 Key Features

- **Hands-Free Voice Interface:** A sleek, single-orb minimalist UI. Tap the orb to converse directly with the engine.
- **Dynamic Excel Integration:** Automatically ingests local customer lead datasets (`leads.xlsx`) to contextually understand who you are visiting.
- **ElevenLabs Voice Synthesis:** Highly realistic, spontaneous human-like voice responses guiding the user through the initial setup and reading the final playbook.
- **Autonomous Multi-Agent Pipeline:** Routes intents and compiles massive amounts of open data into concise, punchy sales strategies on the fly.
- **Smart Auto-Mic:** The microphone intelligently re-activates when the AI expects a conversational answer, and stays off during heavy research phases.

## 🧠 The 4-Agent Pipeline architecture

The core of the Cloover Engine is a multi-agent cascade utilizing ultra-fast models to synthesize a bespoke playbook in seconds.

1. **Market Intelligence Agent:** Analyzes the energy market, local PVGIS solar potential, SMARD prices, and regional subsidies based purely on the client's location.
2. **Offer Strategy Agent:** Ingests the market data to determine the absolute best technical fit and product recommendation, predicting technical objections.
3. **Financing Strategy Agent:** Figures out how the customer can actually pay for it—optimizing for Loans, Leasing, and regional incentives (e.g., KfW/BAFA) instead of upfront cash.
4. **Master Sales Coach (Synthesis Agent):** The master orchestrator that synthesizes the three independent reports into a unified, punchy Sales Playbook. It produces an easy-to-read markdown framework alongside a 30-second conversational audio script ready to be spoken to the sales rep.

## 🛠️ Technologies Used

- **Frontend core:** Vanilla HTML5, CSS3 (Glassmorphism design), and JavaScript.
- **Speech Integration:** Web Speech API for voice recognition and **ElevenLabs API** for state-of-the-art text-to-speech feedback.
- **LLM Backbone:** Direct integration with the **Google Gemini API** (`gemini-flash-lite-latest`) for parallel high-speed agentic reasoning.
- **Data Parsing:** `SheetJS` CDN integration to dynamically parse local `.xlsx` lead sheets on runtime.

## 💻 Running Locally

To avoid restrictive browser CORS errors when fetching the local `.xlsx` files and audio components:

1. Open your terminal in the application directory.
2. Run a local development server:
   ```bash
   python3 -m http.server 8080
   ```
3. Open your browser and navigate to `http://localhost:8080`.
4. Ensure your microphone permissions are granted when clicking the Orb for the first time.

content.text:
`209fce9` is on GitHub now. Here's what's in it and how it compares with what I built.

## What's in `209fce9`
A merge of `main` into `feature_v` (15 files, +470 / −50). Most of that is your work coming in from `main`: the Conflict block, Happiness Meter and conflict tests. Vishwa's own new changes are small:

| Piece | Vishwa's version | Mine (PR #22) |
|---|---|---|
| **Market conflict flag** | Amber fill, the **same style as "Weak evidence"**, so the two look alike | Orange outline, clearly different |
| **Conflict filter** | None | "Market conflicts" option in the AI-recommendation filter |
| **Happiness Meter on the board** | Our full Data-health meter, including the **sales-weighted total**. **Only appears when one car is selected**, since coverage is measured per car | Compact strip of four bars. Also on the all-cars board (counts combined), but **no sales-weighted total** |

**My take:** keep my flag and filter. For the meter, his reasoning is sound and the weighted total is useful. I'd combine the two: my compact strip on the all-cars board, and his full meter with the weighted total when one car is selected. That's about 10 minutes. Want it?

## Two problems in his commit
1. **It has a "Co-Authored-By: Claude" line**, which breaks the team rule of no AI attribution in commits. It's now in `feature_v`'s history, so if `feature_v` is ever merged, that line ends up in `main`.
2. **It retires Arjun's Kanban.** Its message says his board "stays the primary view" and removes `kanban.spec.ts`, which goes against what's merged in `main` (#20). PR #22 keeps both: Arjun's priority board on Requirements, and Vishwa's decision board on `/board` and the Decisions tab. Vishwa should know that, so the two branches stop pulling in opposite directions.

## Minerva voice (from your other request)
I read the whole repo: `script.js` is 479 lines of browser speech recognition, ElevenLabs text-to-speech and a 4-agent Gemini pipeline. Three ideas carry over:

1. **Voice that works without an OpenAI key.** Minerva uses the browser's built-in speech recognition plus a local "fast intercept" that answers common commands without an LLM. Our microphone just says "not configured" without a key. With this, simple commands like "open the 7 Series", "show conflicts" or "challenge this" would work in the demo using our existing voice tools and Confirm dialogs. One caveat: Chrome sends that audio to Google for recognition.
2. **Hands-free reopen.** When Minerva finishes speaking, the microphone reopens automatically. That would help in the fallback mode. Our OpenAI mode already listens continuously.
3. **A separate short spoken script.** The model writes the detailed text for the screen plus a short `<voice_script>` to read aloud. That fits our "explain this requirement" answers.

Not useful here: ElevenLabs (yet another third-party service and key) and the Gemini model race (it's for text generation, not voice).

Should I build #1 and #2 into PR #22 as the no-key voice fallback?

content.text:
An ElevenLabs key changes the plan for the better. Here's what I'll build:

- **Voice that works without OpenAI.** The browser's speech recognition hears the command. A local command router (Minerva's "fast intercept") maps it to our existing voice tools, so every action is still audited and decisions or Challenge still need a Confirm click.
- **ElevenLabs reads the answer aloud**, through a server route. Minerva put its key in the browser where anyone could read it; ours stays on the server.
- **Hands-free:** after it speaks, the microphone reopens, as in Minerva.
- If an OpenAI key is ever added, the full conversational agent takes over automatically.

The ElevenLabs voice mode is built and pushed to PR #22 (commit `5457e41`), but it hasn't spoken through ElevenLabs yet because **the key isn't on the server**. Here's what I took from Minerva, and the one step only you can do.

## What I built
- **The mic now works without an OpenAI key.** Your browser's speech recognition hears one command, and a command router like Minerva's "fast intercept" turns it into one of PMW's existing voice actions. No AI model is involved.
- **Commands it understands:**
  - "open the 7 Series", "show the 5 Series decision matrix"
  - "go to the requirements board", "open the radar", "show the audit trail"
  - "show conflicts", "which quick wins does the 1 Series have"
  - "explain the score", "read me a customer quote"
  - "challenge this", "approve this", "reject this"
  - "give me my briefing", "what should I look at", "missing voices"
  - "stop"
- **ElevenLabs reads the answer aloud**, with Minerva's voice (Adam) and model (turbo v2.5). Unlike Minerva, **the key stays on the server**; Minerva put it in the browser where anyone could read it.
- **Hands-free:** after replying, the mic opens again, as in Minerva. It waits instead if a Confirm dialog is open.
- **Same safety as before:** every command is region-filtered and audited, and approve or Challenge still need your Confirm click.
- If an OpenAI key is ever added, the full conversational agent takes over automatically.
- **Bug fixed along the way:** "challenge this" would have hit the **first card in the list** instead of the requirement you have open.

**Checks:** 53 / 53 browser tests and 18 / 18 voice unit tests pass, plus typecheck, lint and build. Retrieves and queries up-to-date documentation and code examples from Context7 for any programming library or framework.

You must call 'Resolve Context7 Library ID' tool first to obtain the exact Context7-compatible library ID required to use this tool, UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question.

If you know the programming language the user is working in, pass it as `language` so the results match their setup.

libraryId.description: Exact Context7-compatible library ID (e.g., '/mongodb/docs', '/vercel/next.js', '/supabase/supabase', '/vercel/next.js/v14.3.0-canary.87') retrieved from 'resolve-library-id' or directly from user query in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version'.

query.description: What to look up in the library's documentation, scoped to a single concept. Be specific and include relevant details, but keep each query to one topic — if the user's question spans multiple distinct concepts, make a separate call per concept instead of combining them, unless the question is about how the concepts interact. Good: 'How to set up authentication with JWT in Express.js' or 'React useEffect cleanup function examples'. Bad (too vague): 'auth' or 'hooks'. Bad (too broad): 'routing and auth and caching in Next.js'. The query is sent to the Context7 API for processing. Do not include any sensitive or confidential information such as API keys, passwords, credentials, personal data, or proprietary code in your query.

language.description: Programming language the user is writing code in, such as 'Python', 'TypeScript', 'Go', or 'C#'. Ranks code examples in that language first. Leave it out when the language is unknown or does not apply.

entries.name: mcp__plugin_context7_context7__resolve-library-id
entries.description:
Resolves a package/product name to a Context7-compatible library ID and returns matching libraries.

You MUST call this function before 'Query Documentation' tool to obtain a valid Context7-compatible library ID UNLESS the user explicitly provides a library ID in the format '/org/project' or '/org/project/version' in their query.

Each result includes:
- Library ID: Context7-compatible identifier (format: /org/project)
- Name: Library or package name
- Description: Short summary
- Code Snippets: Number of available code examples
- Source Reputation: Authority indicator (High, Medium, Low, or Unknown)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)
- Versions: List of versions if available. Use one of those versions if the user provides a version in their query. The format of the version is /org/project/version.

For best results, select libraries based on name match, source reputation, snippet coverage, benchmark score, and relevance to your use case.

Selection Process:
1. Analyze the query to understand what library/package the user is looking for
2. Return the most relevant match based on:
- Name similarity to the query (exact matches prioritized)
- Description relevance to the query's intent
- Documentation coverage (prioritize libraries with higher Code Snippet counts)
- Source reputation (consider libraries with High or Medium reputation more authoritative)
- Benchmark Score: Quality indicator (100 is the highest score)

Response Format:
- Return the selected library ID in a clearly marked section
- Provide a brief explanation for why this library was chosen
- If multiple good matches exist, acknowledge this but proceed with the most relevant one
- If no good matches exist, clearly state this and suggest query refinements

For ambiguous queries, request clarification before proceeding with a best-guess match.

IMPORTANT: Do not call this tool more than 3 times per question. If you cannot find what you need after 3 calls, use the best result you have.

content.text:
### POST /v1/convai/agents/create

Source: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/api-reference/agents/create

Creates a new conversational agent with the specified configuration.

```APIDOC
## POST /v1/convai/agents/create

### Description
Create an agent from a config object.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/create

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **enable_versioning** (boolean) - Optional - Deprecated: all agents are versioned. This parameter is ignored.

#### Request Body
- **conversation_config** (object) - Required - Conversation configuration for an agent
  - **asr** (object) - Optional - Configuration for conversational transcription
    - **quality** ("high") - Optional - The quality of the transcription
    - **provider** (enum) - Optional - The provider of the transcription service (elevenlabs, scribe_realtime)
    - **user_input_audio_format** (enum) - Optional - The format of the audio to be transcribed (pcm_8000, pcm_16000, pcm_22050, pcm_24000, pcm_44100, pcm_48000, ulaw_8000)
    - **keywords** (list of string) - Optional - Keywords to boost prediction probability for
  - **turn** (object) - Optional - Configuration for turn detection
    - **turn_timeout** (double) - Optional - Maximum wait time for the user's reply before re-engaging the user
    - **initial_wait_time** (double) - Optional - How long the agent will wait for the user to start the conversation if the first message is empty
    - **silence_end_call_timeout** (double) - Optional - Maximum wait time since the user last spoke before terminating the call
    - **turn_eagerness** (enum) - Optional - Controls how eager the agent is to respond (patient, normal, eager)
    - **spelling_patience** (enum) - Optional - Controls if the agent should be more patient when user is spelling numbers and named entities (auto, off)
    - **speculative_turn** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, starts generating LLM responses during silence before full turn confidence is reached
    - **retranscribe_on_turn_timeout** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, if VAD detects no speech, attempts to re-transcribe accumulated audio at turn timeout
    - **turn_model** (enum) - Optional - Version of the turn detection model to use (turn_v2, turn_v3)
    - **interruption_ignore_terms** (list of string) - Optional - List of terms that should not trigger an interruption
    - **interruption_ignore_term_languages** (list of string) - Optional - Language codes for which preset ignore-term categories have been activated
    - **merge_with_default_ignore_terms** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, the curated default terms for interruption_ignore_term_languages are used in addition to interruption_ignore_terms
    - **transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions** (boolean) - Optional - When interruptions are disabled, still transcribe what the user says
    - **soft_timeout_config** (object) - Optional - Configuration for soft timeout functionality
      - **timeout_seconds** (double) - Optional - Time in seconds before showing the predefined message while waiting for LLM response
      - **message** (string) - Optional - Message to show when the first soft timeout is reached
```

--------------------------------

### POST /v1/convai/tools

Source: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/api-reference/tools/create

Creates a new tool configuration for use in conversational agents.

```APIDOC
## POST /v1/convai/tools

### Description
Creates a new tool configuration for the Conversational AI service.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/tools

### Request Body
- **tool_config** (object) - Required - The configuration object for the tool.
  - **type** (string) - Required - The type of the tool (e.g., "client").
  - **description** (string) - Required - A description of the tool's purpose.
  - **name** (string) - Required - The name of the tool.
  - **expects_response** (boolean) - Required - Whether the tool expects a response.
```

## ConversationClient.startSession

### Description
Initiates the WebRTC connection and starts using the microphone to communicate with the ElevenLabs Agents agent.

### Method Signature
`ConversationClient.startSession(config: ConversationConfig, context: Context): ConversationSession`

### Parameters

  - **agentId** (`String`) - Optional (Required for public agents) - The unique identifier of the agent obtained from the ElevenLabs UI.

        userId = "your-user-id"

    context = this
)

val session = ConversationClient.startSession(
    config = ConversationConfig(
        conversationToken = conversationToken
    ),
    context = this

### POST /v1/convai/agents/create

Source: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/api-reference/agents/create

Creates a new conversational agent with the specified configuration.

```APIDOC
## POST /v1/convai/agents/create

### Description
Create an agent from a config object.

### Method
POST

### Endpoint
https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/create

### Parameters
#### Query Parameters
- **enable_versioning** (boolean) - Optional - Deprecated: all agents are versioned. This parameter is ignored.

#### Request Body
- **conversation_config** (object) - Required - Conversation configuration for an agent
  - **asr** (object) - Optional - Configuration for conversational transcription
    - **quality** ("high") - Optional - The quality of the transcription
    - **provider** (enum) - Optional - The provider of the transcription service (elevenlabs, scribe_realtime)
    - **user_input_audio_format** (enum) - Optional - The format of the audio to be transcribed (pcm_8000, pcm_16000, pcm_22050, pcm_24000, pcm_44100, pcm_48000, ulaw_8000)
    - **keywords** (list of string) - Optional - Keywords to boost prediction probability for
  - **turn** (object) - Optional - Configuration for turn detection
    - **turn_timeout** (double) - Optional - Maximum wait time for the user's reply before re-engaging the user
    - **initial_wait_time** (double) - Optional - How long the agent will wait for the user to start the conversation if the first message is empty
    - **silence_end_call_timeout** (double) - Optional - Maximum wait time since the user last spoke before terminating the call
    - **turn_eagerness** (enum) - Optional - Controls how eager the agent is to respond (patient, normal, eager)
    - **spelling_patience** (enum) - Optional - Controls if the agent should be more patient when user is spelling numbers and named entities (auto, off)
    - **speculative_turn** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, starts generating LLM responses during silence before full turn confidence is reached
    - **retranscribe_on_turn_timeout** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, if VAD detects no speech, attempts to re-transcribe accumulated audio at turn timeout
    - **turn_model** (enum) - Optional - Version of the turn detection model to use (turn_v2, turn_v3)
    - **interruption_ignore_terms** (list of string) - Optional - List of terms that should not trigger an interruption
    - **interruption_ignore_term_languages** (list of string) - Optional - Language codes for which preset ignore-term categories have been activated
    - **merge_with_default_ignore_terms** (boolean) - Optional - When enabled, the curated default terms for interruption_ignore_term_languages are used in addition to interruption_ignore_terms
    - **transcribe_on_disabled_interruptions** (boolean) - Optional - When interruptions are disabled, still transcribe what the user says
    - **soft_timeout_config** (object) - Optional - Configuration for soft timeout functionality
      - **timeout_seconds** (double) - Optional - Time in seconds before showing the predefined message while waiting for LLM response
      - **message** (string) - Optional - Message to show when the first soft timeout is reached
```
